Today's release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 includes a brand new dynamic wallpaper featuring the Golden Gate Bridge, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. All of them are available for download below.

The macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper gallery continues to expand

When Apple announced macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, it showcased the same system wallpaper across all operating systems, featuring a stylized number 27.

However, after several developer beta versions, Apple began adding dynamic scenes that can serve as both screen savers and wallpapers, offering slow-motion aerial views of San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge.

When the Mac is unlocked, the screen saver gradually comes to a stop, each time leaving behind a slightly different new wallpaper.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, below you can find a static screenshot gallery of the four videos, along with the light and dark versions of the universal stylized 27 wallpaper.

Be sure to click the images to save the full-resolution versions. To set them as your background, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to "Your Photos," click the Add Photo button, then you can follow any of the methods below:

Add a photo from your Photos library: Click "Choose from Photos," then select a photo. Add an image file: Click "Choose File," select a file, then click "Open." You can also drag images from your Desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: Click "Choose Folder," select a folder, then click "Open." Add an album or folder from the Photos app: Select an album or folder under "Photo Library."

According to Apple, "You can also customize your wallpaper without opening Wallpaper Settings":

Use a photo from your Photos library: Go to the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click "Set as Wallpaper." Use an image found online: In a Safari window, Control-click the image, then select "Use Image as Desktop Picture." Use an image saved on your Mac: Click the Finder in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click "Set Desktop Picture."

To learn more about ways to set custom wallpaper in macOS, click this link.
